_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for GOOG retrospectives (retro/build_goog.py), generated from Google's own filings: every raw figure is the row string it appears in (kept in 'rows'), checked against its filing, and every growth rate, margin, gap and rule-T value is computed from those figures. Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date (EDGAR's acceptance time; after the 16:00 ET close, the next trading day). Dollar figures in thousands as the filings print them ('_k'); per-share figures as published (no split before 2010).

history_vintages.why: 'Google is a global technology leader focused on improving the ways people connect with information.' 'We generate our revenue almost entirely from advertising, and the reduction in spending by or loss of advertisers could seriously harm our business.' 'We face significant competition from Microsoft and Yahoo.' 'As our growth rate has slowed, the cyclicality and seasonality in our business has become more pronounced and will cause our operating results to fluctuate in the future.' (FY2006 10-K); CYCLICAL: the 10-K says so of its own business ('the cyclicality and seasonality in our business'), the BKR, CAT and NVDA reading, not an industry's words; no theme in taxonomy_eras.json is live for a search and advertising company on these dates (OFFSHORE is scoped to IT services), so the watch list is empty; the competitors named are a competitive field, not a theme, and stay here (the PEP obesity rule)

revenue.measure: revenue growth, % (each pair of years from the latest filing published by 2008-01-04 that reports both: the 424B4 for 1999-2000, the FY2004 10-K for 2000-2001, the FY2005 10-K for 2001-2002, the FY2006 10-K for 2002-2006)

gross_margin.measure: change in (revenues less cost of revenues) / revenues, bp, the same filings: cost of revenues as published (stock-based compensation a separate line in the 424B4 and the FY2004 and FY2005 10-Ks, allocated to cost of revenues in the FY2006 10-K's restated 2002-2006: a seam, as published)

opex_gap.measure: growth of research and development plus sales and marketing plus general and administrative less revenue growth, pp (lower is better), the same filings; the separate stock-based compensation, Yahoo settlement and Google Foundation lines are not in it

op_margin.measure: change in operating income / revenues, bp, the same filings as revenue; GAAP as published (the 2004 Yahoo settlement and the 2005 Google Foundation contribution in operating income)

receivables_gap.measure: growth of year-end accounts receivable, net, less revenue growth, pp (lower is better), each pair of year ends from the latest filing published by 2008-01-04 whose balance sheet reports both (the 424B4 for 2002-2003, the FY2004, FY2005 and FY2006 10-Ks after), with that filing's revenues
